column1: # Checks in this pack that are DECLARED UNPRICED.
# A check with an all-zero frequency triple contributes exactly nothing to
# reported exposure however often it fails. That is a legitimate state -- a
# magnitude without a calibrated frequency is not a price -- but it must be
# SAID, not inferred from a field of zeros. pricing-test.sh fails any check
# that is neither priced nor listed here, so the silence cannot return.
# Every check in v1.0 (7 of 7) and v2.0 (19 of 19) is in this state, and from
# 2026-10-11 so are 5 of the 11 checks in v2.1. The v2.1 five are a different
# case and carry a different reason code: they were priced, and they were moved
# off the technical loss path because a documentation gap does not cause a
# technical loss event. They defend against a PENALTY. See
# REASON CODES. This is the allow-list. pricing-test.sh fails any other value.
#   no-calibrated-frequency      Carries a magnitude but no calibrated annual
#                                frequency. Calibration is the principal's call.
#   placeholder-not-evaluated    status: placeholder. The check is never
#                                evaluated, so zero exposure is correct.
#   penalty-path-not-technical   The control defends against a statutory penalty
#                                rather than against a technical loss event.
#                                Pricing it needs the secondary-loss model that
#                                section 4 describes and the engine lacks.
# Each check in v1.0 and v2.0 now also writes "freqTriple": {"min": 0,
# "mode": 0, "max": 0} into framework.json, so the zero is declared in the
# pack data as well as here rather than arriving as a Go zero value. An
# `unpriced` schema key cannot be used: the loader runs DisallowUnknownFields,
# so a new key breaks pack loading.
# Removing a line requires adding a real freqTriple to that check, and the
# test fails a line whose check has since been priced, so this list cannot rot.
# Calibration is the principal's call. Do not invent triples to empty this file.

Moved off the technical loss path on 2026-10-11. This control defends against a statutory penalty, not against a breach: a documentation or transparency gap does not cause a technical loss event. Its previous frequency asserted that it did. The ceiling is EU AI Act Art. 99(4), EUR 15m or 3 per cent, and a ceiling is a max rather than a mode. Pricing it needs the secondary-loss model the engine does not have. See ../../ANCHORS.md and ../../PENALTIES.md.
